authority: CEO Round 154: 'Build Competitive White-Space Engine. For every competitor: CAPABILITY → GAP → DESIGN-AROUND → BUYER NEED → INVENTION HYPOTHESIS.'

white_space_engine.design: For each competitor, map what they have, what they're missing, what they could copy, what they cannot copy, what they would buy, and what would make them buy NOW. Then generate invention hypotheses from the gaps.

what_they_are_actively_building: Likely: chronic safety, longer in-vivo duration, more patients
what_they_appear_to_be_missing: Latent degradation detection (no longitudinal failure prediction)
Failure-mode classification (obstruction vs overdrainage vs fracture vs migration)
Early warning with clinically meaningful lead time
what_they_could_copy: Pressure-based threshold alarms (simple, already have pressure sensor)
Basic trend detection (could add software to existing hardware)
what_they_cannot_easily_copy: Validated longitudinal response-manifold model (requires months/years of patient data + validated degradation model)
Failure-mode classification from response kinetics (requires clinical correlation + multi-failure-mode training data)
Patient-specific degradation trajectory (requires proprietary longitudinal calibration protocol)
Predictive lead-time advantage (requires validated prediction model, not just control)
what_they_would_likely_buy: A validated failure-prediction layer that sits above their control system
A failure-mode classifier that improves their diagnostic value proposition
A patient-specific calibration protocol that makes their shunt 'smart' over months, not just minutes
what_would_make_them_buy_now: If they are moving toward clinical trials, regulatory bodies may require failure-detection capability. A validated prediction layer could become a regulatory differentiator.
If competing smart-shunt programs (e.g., CereVasc with intelligence layer) emerge, VIEshunt's control-only approach becomes commoditized.
invention_hypotheses_from_gap: C2-Y: Longitudinal Response-Manifold Failure Prediction (lead-time advantage over control-only systems)
C1-X: Predictive Shunt Failure Engine (failure-mode classification + prediction)
competitor_objects.design_around_risk: MEDIUM-HIGH — VIEshunt could add basic threshold alarms easily. But validated longitudinal degradation prediction requires accumulated patient data + clinical correlation that takes years to build.
competitor_objects.buyer_fit: MEDIUM — VIEshunt is academic. But whoever commercializes VIEshunt-like technology (CereVasc, Medtronic, Integra) would want the intelligence layer.
competitor_objects.time_to_value: 2-3 years (requires longitudinal clinical data for validation)

what_they_have: Endovascular transdural CSF shunt (IPS to CPA cistern)
what_they_appear_to_be_missing: Any sensing or intelligence (current eShunt is passive drainage)
what_they_could_copy: Add a pressure sensor to the eShunt (hardware modification)
what_they_cannot_easily_copy: Validated intelligence/prediction layer (requires AI + clinical data + validation)
Closed-loop drug delivery (requires C3 therapeutic platform + regulatory path)
Thrombus risk monitoring (requires C5 physics + multi-world validation)
Longitudinal patient-specific model (requires accumulated data + validation)
what_they_would_likely_buy: An intelligence layer (C1-X/C2-Y) that makes eShunt 'smart' — transforms passive drainage into predictive monitoring
A drug delivery capability (C3-X) that expands eShunt's indications beyond NPH
A thrombus risk monitor (C5-X) that addresses eShunt-specific safety concerns
A platform moat: eShunt + sensing + prediction + delivery + thrombus monitoring = neurovascular intelligence OS
what_would_make_them_buy_now: STRIDE data publication may reveal failure modes that need addressing → intelligence layer becomes urgent
J&J/Medtronic investment creates pressure for platform expansion beyond single-indication device
Competitor pressure from VIEshunt-like systems → CereVasc needs intelligence to maintain differentiation
PMA review may require post-market surveillance plan → predictive monitoring adds value
invention_hypotheses_from_gap: C1-X: eShunt-specific predictive failure engine (integrates with eShunt anatomy)
C2-Y: Response-manifold prediction on eShunt platform
C3-X: Closed-loop CNS delivery via eShunt (expands indications)
C5-X: Embolic risk monitoring for eShunt patients (safety enhancement)
competitor_objects.design_around_risk: LOW for eShunt-specific inventions (unique anatomy). HIGH for generic shunt intelligence.
competitor_objects.buyer_fit: VERY HIGH — CereVasc is the primary platform. Any intelligence/delivery/safety layer is more valuable integrated with eShunt than standalone.

what_they_are_actively_building: Clinical validation of ThecaFlex for chronic intrathecal dosing
Likely: expanded indications (ALS, SMA, gene therapy)
what_they_appear_to_be_missing: Adaptive delivery based on measured response
what_they_could_copy: Add a pressure sensor to ThecaFlex (hardware modification)
Partner with a monitoring company for external sensing
what_they_cannot_easily_copy: Validated closed-loop CNS delivery algorithm (requires CSF pharmacokinetic model + clinical validation)
Physiology-aware dosing (requires real-time CSF state estimation + drug response model)
Patient-specific drug-delivery digital twin (requires accumulated response data + validated model)
what_they_would_likely_buy: A closed-loop delivery intelligence layer that makes ThecaFlex 'smart' — transforms open-loop port into adaptive therapy system
A CSF-state monitoring capability that enables physiology-aware dosing
A patient-specific pharmacokinetic model that optimizes dosing per individual
what_would_make_them_buy_now: If ThecaFlex clinical trials show variable patient response → adaptive dosing becomes essential
If competing CNS delivery platforms add intelligence → Biogen needs to differentiate
If gene therapy delivery requires precise dosing control → closed-loop becomes regulatory requirement
invention_hypotheses_from_gap: C3-X: Closed-loop CNS delivery with physiological feedback
C3-Y: Patient-specific CSF pharmacokinetic digital twin for dosing optimization
competitor_objects.design_around_risk: MEDIUM — ThecaFlex already provides access. C3-X's advantage must be in INTELLIGENCE, not hardware.
competitor_objects.buyer_fit: VERY HIGH — Biogen paid $85M for the platform. A validated intelligence layer could be worth more to them than standalone.

what_they_cannot_easily_copy: Multi-parameter response-manifold model (requires fusion of pressure + flow + posture + perturbation, not just pressure)
Validated failure prediction (requires longitudinal clinical data + model)
what_they_would_likely_buy: An inference layer that transforms their pressure data into actionable predictions
A multi-parameter fusion model that makes their sensor more valuable

what_would_make_them_buy_now: If their sensor is approved but clinicians ask 'what do I do with the data?' → inference layer becomes essential

invention_hypotheses_from_gap: C2-Y: Response-manifold model that uses ICP monitor data as input
C1-X: Predictive failure engine that fuses ICP monitor + shunt telemetry
competitor_objects.design_around_risk: HIGH for sensing hardware. LOW for inference layer (requires validated model, not just data).
competitor_objects.buyer_fit: HIGH — they have the sensor, we have the brain. Partnership/acquisition of inference layer makes their product dramatically more valuable.

c2_y_vieshunt_attack.scientific_question: Can latent degradation prediction provide a measurable lead-time advantage over the capabilities already demonstrated by intelligent/adaptive shunt systems (VIEshunt)?
c2_y_vieshunt_attack.what_vieshunt_demonstrates: Reactive control: posture → adjust reference → regulate ICP. Acute perturbation → measure response → adapt.
c2_y_vieshunt_attack.what_c2_y_proposes: Predictive monitoring: perturbation → measure response → compare to longitudinal baseline → detect deviation → predict failure before clinical symptoms.
c2_y_vieshunt_attack.key_distinction: VIEshunt controls CURRENT state. C2-Y predicts FUTURE failure. These are materially different technical goals.
c2_y_vieshunt_attack.experiment_required: C2-Y-R1: Virtual cohort with gradual degradation. Compare detection lead time: (A) static pressure threshold, (B) VIEshunt-like adaptive control deviation, (C) C2-Y response-manifold deviation. Measure: median lead time, false alarms/patient-month, failure-mode accuracy.

pre_registered_thresholds.win: C2-Y detects degradation >24 hours before static threshold AND false alarm rate <1/patient-month
pre_registered_thresholds.kill: C2-Y provides <4 hours lead-time advantage OR false alarm rate >3/patient-month

c3_thecaflex_attack.scientific_question: What clinically meaningful capability would make Biogen pay for an additional intelligence layer rather than simply use ThecaFlex as-is?
c3_thecaflex_attack.what_thecaflex_demonstrates: Open-loop intrathecal access: clinician programs dose → ThecaFlex delivers. No feedback, no adaptation, no CSF-state awareness.
c3_thecaflex_attack.what_c3_x_proposes: Closed-loop delivery: CSF state → pharmacokinetic model → adaptive dosing → response monitoring → dose adjustment.
c3_thecaflex_attack.key_distinction: ThecaFlex is a PORT. C3-X is a THERAPY SYSTEM. The port is hardware; the intelligence is the moat.
c3_thecaflex_attack.buyer_value_chain: Biogen paid $85M for the port. A validated closed-loop layer could: (1) expand indications (precision dosing for gene therapy), (2) improve safety (avoid over/under-dosing), (3) create data moat (accumulated patient-specific pharmacokinetic data), (4) regulatory differentiation (adaptive dosing as safety feature).
c3_thecaflex_attack.experiment_required: C3-X-R1: Virtual cohort comparing open-loop vs closed-loop CNS delivery. Measure: drug concentration stability, over/under-dosing events, patient-specific optimization benefit.

moat_taxonomy.technical_moat: Validated mechanism that survives independent reproduction (C5 precursor, C2-Y response-manifold)
moat_taxonomy.data_moat: Accumulated longitudinal patient-specific calibration data (C2-Y baseline, C3-X pharmacokinetic)
moat_taxonomy.model_moat: Validated prediction model that competitors cannot reproduce without equivalent data + validation
moat_taxonomy.workflow_moat: Integration into clinical workflow (sense → predict → decide → intervene → monitor → learn)
moat_taxonomy.integration_moat: Platform plays (eShunt + intelligence + delivery + thrombus monitoring = neurovascular OS)
moat_taxonomy.ip_moat: Patents on specific validated mechanisms (not generic concepts)
